messages:
maya: Quick update from the mariner-14b bring-up. Ran two quant profiles (int6-conservative, int4-compact) across three slices: search-short, chat-multi, and rerank. Pulling top-line econ + quality.

omar: Nice  what were the evaluation metrics?

maya: Metrics = BLEU-ish similarity proxy, pairwise rerank A/B win-rate, hallucination-rate, median latency p95, and end-to-end cost/token. Short summary: int6 sim=0.915, int4 sim=0.885. Rerank win-rate (vs opt13b baseline) int6=52%, int4=48%. Cost/token: int6=$0.0032, int4=$0.0021.

jin: So roughly 34% cost reduction for int4 but 3% relative downgrade in sim and 4pp hit on rerank wins. Any slice-specific failures?

maya: Yes. chat-multi (avg prompt size ~6k) shows the largest gap: sim drop = 0.04 absolute and hallucination-rate up 1.8x for int4. search-short is fine. rerank had more false positives with int4 on paraphrase-heavy queries.

opsbot: infra-bot: kv-cache stability warning for int4 runs  observed cache fragmentation on 12% of sessions (triggered 3725002500).

omar: Did you test warmstart (cached prefixes) vs cold sessions?

maya: We did. Warmstart masks most quality issues: for cached sessions int4 sim -> 0.905, close to int6. Cold-start scenarios are where int4 struggles. Suggests prefix integrity loss.

jin: From an econ perspective, if traffic is 70% warmstart, effective cost savings for int4 is only ~18% after accounting for increased re-runs and manual review.

maya: I uploaded a compact scorecard: /shared/eval/mariner-14b/3725001111-scorecard.csv (link). Also attached a short config snippet we used: 

```json
{
  "model": "mariner-14b",
  "profiles": ["int6-conservative","int4-compact"],
  "slices": ["search-short","chat-multi","rerank"],
  "kv_cache": "enabled",
  "tokenization": "bpe-v2"
}
```

tara-product: For GTN the ask is: recommended default + fallback. Product wants to avoid regressions on chat. Baseline requirement: sim >= 0.90 on chat-multi.

eileen: Ops proposal: route by warmstart-status + slice. Pseudocode: if slice=="chat-multi" and warmstart==false -> use int6; else try int4. Canary at 5% first then ramp. Add alerting on rerank win-rate drop >3pp.

omar: Agree. Also propose hybrid prefix scheme: serve first 512 tokens on int6 then switch to int4. Early tests show hybrid recovers ~70% of the quality gap for chat-multi while keeping ~20% cost savings vs full int6.

jin: That hybrid idea seems promising. Can we simulate token distribution to estimate break-even for cost vs quality? If hybrid gives 20% cost reduction and keeps sim >=0.90, it's a win.

maya: I'll run a 10k request hybrid sim tomorrow and post the updated scorecard. Tentative timeline: hybrid sim -> 3725080000, detailed CSV -> /shared/eval/mariner-14b/3725080000-hybrid.csv.

tara-product: Product ok with default=int6 for chat, int4 for search; allow GTN teams to opt-in to hybrid via feature-flag. Please add a one-paragraph note for GTN docs explaining warmstart sensitivity.

eileen: I'll add routing flags: `route.slice_chat_default=int6`, `route.slice_search_default=int4`, `feature.hybrid_prefix=false` default. Ops will own canary and alert thresholds.

opsbot: deploy-bot: feature flags created for mariner routing  created 3725003600

maya: Thanks all. Follow-ups: (1) hybrid run and scorecard, (2) add warmstart detection metric to console, (3) short GTN blurb. Will post results here and close thread when we have hybrid numbers.

omar: Thanks. Keep notes concise. :thumbsup:
